title: More precise movement and manipulation for robots
lead: Signal processing, text memory and whole-body control change different parts of a robot's work. This issue places those methods alongside a factory pilot and software reuse.

news.title: Gemini Robotics 2.5 is tested on automotive parts kitting
news.summary: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini Robotics 2.5 for robot action control. An Apptronik–Mercedes-Benz pilot combined it with a separate reasoning model to sort parts using Apollo 2; the developer reports 96% success without a complete trial protocol.
news.details: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini Robotics 2.5 on November 10, a model that chooses robot actions from images and verbal instructions. Its developer evaluated more than 200 distinct tasks, including tool use and flexible objects. A separate pilot with Apptronik and Mercedes-Benz used Apollo 2 humanoids to pick metal automotive fastening parts, or brackets, from bins and place them in a required sequence. Trials took place on active production lines in Kecskemét, Hungary, and Sindelfingen, Germany. The company reports 96% task success for that pilot, without giving a total attempt count in the announcement.

news.body:
A new model is best examined through its specific control chain. Google DeepMind's announcement contains both individual-task evaluations and a production pilot using two software levels. That separation matters for reproduction: a whole-system result cannot automatically be assigned to the movement module alone. Task selection, execution and completion checking each need an identifiable role.

Its developer evaluated more than 200 distinct tasks, including tool use and flexible objects. A separate pilot with Apptronik and Mercedes-Benz used Apollo 2 humanoids to pick metal automotive fastening parts, or brackets, from bins and place them in a required sequence. Trials took place on active production lines in Kecskemét, Hungary, and Sindelfingen, Germany. The company reports 96% task success for that pilot, without giving a total attempt count in the announcement.

The system separates two levels: Gemini Robotics ER tracks the workflow, while the new action model controls the hands and arms. The production result therefore belongs to that configuration, rather than to one isolated neural network. Laboratory comparisons also vary by task: sweeping rubbish into a dustpan improved from 0% to 52% against Gemini Robotics 2, for example. The model is rolling out to robotics partners. These are developer-reported figures, without independent assessment, a complete human-intervention record or a cost per handled part in the release.

Comparison with another installation needs the bracket-kitting protocol, rather than an average across two hundred heterogeneous tasks.

news.title: PRISM improves control by changing neural-network input processing
news.summary: Michigan researchers presented PRISM at the Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) to learn combinations of measurements and commands. Improvements appear in simulated walking and a separate physical grasp test; the original preprint dates to July.
news.details: The University of Michigan presented PRISM at the Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) in Austin on November 10. It is an input component for a movement-control neural network. The preprint first appeared in July; the current event is its conference presentation, not a new original-publication date. PRISM learns useful multiplicative combinations of observations, previous actions and commands, such as joint-position and velocity signals. Replacing initial input processing lets it fit existing learning systems without a new training objective or extra sensors. Its contribution is a change in representation rather than simply a larger parameter count.

news.body:
A controller receives positions, velocities and commands, yet useful information can depend on their combinations. PRISM makes those combinations a learned part of its input representation. This is a targeted component replacement rather than a new robot architecture. A conventional network of matching size is consequently an informative comparison: it asks whether extra parameters alone would suffice.

The preprint first appeared in July; the current event is its conference presentation, not a new original-publication date. PRISM learns useful multiplicative combinations of observations, previous actions and commands, such as joint-position and velocity signals. Replacing initial input processing lets it fit existing learning systems without a new training objective or extra sensors. Its contribution is a change in representation rather than simply a larger parameter count.

In simulation, humanoids completed 92.5% of 24-second trials without falling, against 51% for a conventional network. Enlarging the conventional network to a comparable size produced 52.3%. This measures stability over a fixed interval, not long-term service lifetime. In a separate physical test, an SO-101 arm picked up a roll of tape with 94% success across 50 attempts, against 68% using identical training demonstrations. The university reports its team's results. Simulated walking and physical grasping percentages belong to separate experiments, not one general reliability figure.

news.title: RoboScript stores rehearsal experience in text without retraining its base model
news.summary: Huazhong University and ArcheOne AI proposed RoboScript with a task's text memory frozen for evaluation. The 50-task virtual test averaged 83.4% success; that is not the success rate of physical dual-arm trials.
news.details: Researchers at Huazhong University of Science and Technology and ArcheOne AI described RoboScript, a system that improves task execution by writing rehearsal feedback into text memory. The underlying model stays unchanged. Starting from one demonstration, it rehearses in simulation, records useful steps and object roles, and freezes that memory for evaluation on new scenes. The method is called World In-Context Learning: adaptation through information supplied alongside a task, rather than changes to the model's internal parameters.

The underlying model stays unchanged. Starting from one demonstration, it rehearses in simulation, records useful steps and object roles, and freezes that memory for evaluation on new scenes. The method is called World In-Context Learning: adaptation through information supplied alongside a task, rather than changes to the model's internal parameters.
news.engineering_impact: The system is also bounded by its available actions. A record can guide their order without creating a missing movement skill. The authors identify cloth, cables and tightly coordinated two-arm operations as difficult cases. Addressing those cases requires suitable observations, skills and rehearsal environments, rather than simply writing a longer note.
news.limitations: The 83.4% concerns simulated RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, not physical trials. Rehearsals and existing movement skills are required; cloth, cables and close two-arm coordination remain difficult. Independent reproduction is not confirmed.
news.evidence_status: Research and author-run experiments; independent reproduction has not been confirmed.
news.organization: Huazhong University of Science and Technology; ArcheOne AI
news.body:
The changing component here is a task record the model reads when selecting actions. The authors separate rehearsal and evaluation scenes to distinguish accumulated experience from adaptation to the test itself. Text is fixed after preparation. The experiment therefore examines transfer of stored guidance to a new setting, rather than merely correcting a failure already encountered.

The underlying model stays unchanged. Starting from one demonstration, it rehearses in simulation, records useful steps and object roles, and freezes that memory for evaluation on new scenes. The method is called World In-Context Learning: adaptation through information supplied alongside a task, rather than changes to the model's internal parameters.

The preprint appeared on November 9. Across all 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, a virtual suite of dual-arm manipulation, the authors report 83.4% mean success over clean and altered settings. Rehearsal and evaluation scenes are separated; memory is not rewritten for every test episode. Transfer to a physical dual-arm robot is also described, but 83.4% belongs to the virtual suite. Cloth, cables and tightly coordinated two-arm actions remain challenging. Leaving model parameters unchanged does not remove the cost of rehearsals, observations or the pre-existing movement skills used by the system.

The system is also bounded by its available actions. A record can guide their order without creating a missing movement skill. The authors identify cloth, cables and tightly coordinated two-arm operations as difficult cases. Addressing those cases requires suitable observations, skills and rehearsal environments, rather than simply writing a longer note.

news.title: COBRA pushes a box with the same body that moves it
news.summary: Northeastern researchers tested snake-robot box transport without a separate arm. All 20 trials met a 20-centimetre goal tolerance, using external tracking for the robot and cargo positions.
news.details: Northeastern University researchers in Boston presented COBRA, a snake robot that uses the same body for locomotion and pushing a box. It has no separate arm or permanently assigned object-contact section. A geometric planner sets approach and transport paths, while control software adjusts the direction of sidewinding motion. An external motion-capture system supplies robot and box pose. Autonomous action selection in this experiment therefore does not imply independence from laboratory tracking equipment.
news.technical_novelty: Northeastern University researchers in Boston presented COBRA, a snake robot that uses the same body for locomotion and pushing a box. It has no separate arm or permanently assigned object-contact section. A geometric planner sets approach and transport paths, while control software adjusts the direction of sidewinding motion. An external motion-capture system supplies robot and box pose. Autonomous action selection in this experiment therefore does not imply independence from laboratory tracking equipment.
news.engineering_impact: Contact-force optimisation was evaluated separately from the physical control loop. Twenty physical successes therefore do not validate the full contact planner on the machine. They establish delivery into a specified region using selected motion geometry, flat ground and externally measured pose. The 20-centimetre tolerance remains part of any claim about positioning precision.
news.limitations: Twenty trials on flat, rigid ground used a 20 cm goal tolerance and external position tracking. Full contact optimisation was tested separately in simplified simulation, rather than in the complete robot's physical control loop.
news.evidence_status: Research and author-run experiments; independent reproduction has not been confirmed.
news.body:
Moving sections supply both ground support and object contact. The machine therefore cannot be divided in advance into a stationary base and manipulator. Researchers test directional control of this motion while separately developing a fuller physical-contact model. Distinguishing the validated controller from the next planning formulation is more informative than the broad word autonomous.

It has no separate arm or permanently assigned object-contact section. A geometric planner sets approach and transport paths, while control software adjusts the direction of sidewinding motion. An external motion-capture system supplies robot and box pose. Autonomous action selection in this experiment therefore does not imply independence from laboratory tracking equipment.

The November 6 preprint describes 20 physical trials with different starting configurations and goals. All delivered the box within 20 centimetres of the target. That is the success threshold of a particular experiment on flat rigid ground, not a universal precision guarantee. The authors also model robot–ground and robot–box contact and separately test interaction optimisation in simulation. The full contact optimiser did not yet control the entire physical system in a closed feedback loop. Replacing external tracking with onboard sensing is identified as future work, alongside more integrated contact-aware control.

news.title: Mitsubishi applies shared software to a hospital delivery robot
news.summary: Mitsubishi Electric reported the first RoboPivot application in MELDY hospital-robot development. Its estimated 30% concerns guidance-software development and a verification environment, not faster deliveries.
news.details: Mitsubishi Electric announced the first product application of RoboPivot on November 10. This shared software foundation supports robot development. Subsidiary Mitsubishi Electric Mobility used it for MELDY, a multipurpose hospital delivery robot supplied in November to St. Marianna University Hospital in Japan. Departments developed the foundation collaboratively inside the company, reusing code and experience instead of recreating similar functions. This is called InnerSource: open collaboration practices applied internally, rather than a promise that the entire codebase is publicly available.

news.body:
Code reuse changes more than programming volume: a shared foundation can include prepared verification facilities. Mitsubishi explicitly includes that preparation in its comparison. Reproducing the saving would therefore require the reused components and the development baseline, rather than only the platform name or proof that a robot was delivered.

The company estimates a 30% reduction in software-development lead time. A footnote defines the comparison: developing robot guidance functionality from scratch, including preparation of the verification environment. It does not measure travel speed, delivery volume or hospital staff time saved. A separate goal seeks a 50% reduction in the broader product-development cycle by 2030, with a different scope of comparison. Neither the absolute project duration nor independent verification of the estimated saving is supplied. The delivery announcement and the development estimate describe different outcomes.
